axes.model_access:
**Models come through Amazon Bedrock; several vendors are selectable, but it depends on which tier you buy.**

The free tier can only use open-weight models and Claude Sonnet 4.5.
Premium models (including Auto, Sonnet 5, Opus 5) require a paid tier.

The list on the official models page:

- **Auto** — automatic routing
- **OpenAI** — GPT-5.6 (Sol / Terra / Luna)
- **Anthropic Claude** — Opus 5.5 / 5 / 4.8 / 4.7 / 4.6 / 4.5;
  Sonnet 5.5 / 5 / 4.6 / 4.5 / 4.0; Haiku 4.5

- **Open-weight** — DeepSeek 3.2, MiniMax M2.5 / M2.1, GLM-5, Qwen3 Coder Next

Billing is by credit multiplier: Auto is the 1.0x baseline, GPT-5.6 Sol tops out at 4.4x.

Regionally, GPT-5.6 is always served from the US. The rest follow your profile region (US / EU).
Claude Fable 5.1 is an Enterprise preview.

**Whether you can bring your own API key (BYOK): not stated officially.**

(models and pricing pages checked.)
axes.runtime:
**A standalone desktop IDE; the official wording explicitly says "a desktop development environment built on a VS Code foundation"** — not an extension inside someone else's editor. But the official positioning is "one agent, every surface":
IDE / CLI / Web / Mobile are all front ends of one unified agent harness; local clients go over stdio via the
**Agent Client Protocol (ACP)**, while Web / Mobile connect over WebSocket to cloud sandboxes.
**The IDE and CLI run the harness locally by default**, with tools operating on local files and shell.
Both can also create and attach Cloud Sessions inside cloud sandboxes.
Because the boundary is standard ACP, the official pages say JetBrains IDEs and Zed can also use Kiro as their agent.
axes.local_files:
It reaches your workspace files through the IDE.

**Code understanding has two layers.** The first is built-in Tree-sitter, covering 18 languages,
providing fuzzy symbol search, document outlines, AST structural search and rewrite, and codebase overviews.
These work across surfaces.
The second layer is **LSP (optional)**: find references, go to definition, rename, diagnostics, hover docs —
but only in the IDE and CLI, and you install the language servers yourself.

**Indexing has its own page**: opening a project automatically indexes source, docs, configuration and dependencies;
file changes or external edits trigger incremental re-indexing. Manual Force Re-Index / Rebuild is also available.
To keep the agent off certain files, exclude them with `.kiroignore` (gitignore style).

**Whether the index is uploaded to the cloud: not stated officially.**

(codebase indexing and how-kiro-works pages checked.)
axes.background:
**Close the laptop and the task keeps running — that is its most distinctive point.**

Sessions run in vendor-hosted cloud sandboxes and belong to the **account**, not to one app.
So IDE / CLI / Web / Mobile can all attach to the same session;
you can close the lid and pick it up from your phone or a terminal.

Hard numbers given officially:

- Up to **10** concurrent Cloud Sessions
- Cloud compute carries **no extra charge** (included in existing plans)
- Creating from the IDE needs IDE v1.0.293+; from the CLI needs CLI v2.17+

However, the harness running **locally** still depends on your own machine and stops when you exit.

**Official Cloud sessions page wording**: "The agent keeps working in the sandbox whether or not you're connected"
axes.tools:
Four built-in tool classes: files, shell, web, code.

**The extension mechanisms form a system**, six in total:

- **MCP** — local stdio and remote HTTP/SSE; supports server-provided prompts / resources
  and elicitation; `kiro://` one-click install links

- **Powers** — MCP servers packaged with knowledge, loaded on demand
- **Skills** — open-standard portable instruction packs
- **Custom agents and sub-agents**
- **Specs**
- **Hooks**

The Hook trigger points are fully listed officially: Prompt Submit, Agent Stop, Session Start,
Session End (CLI V3), Agent Spawn, Pre / Post Tool Use,
File Create / Save / Delete, Pre / Post Task Execution, Manual.

The CLI also has headless mode (`--no-interactive`, with an API key) for CI/CD.

**⚠ The Mobile surface does not support MCP or local file tools.**
axes.context:
**Specs are its signature.** Each spec generates three files, following "requirements → design → tasks":

- `requirements.md` (or `bugfix.md`)
- `design.md`
- `tasks.md` — supports wave-parallel execution along the dependency graph

**Steering provides persistent project context.** It lives in two places: workspace `.kiro/steering/`,
global `~/.kiro/steering/`. Three base files ship built in: product / tech / structure.
Four inclusion modes are supported — always / fileMatch / manual / auto — and `AGENTS.md` is compatible.

Other context-related capabilities: subagents (each with its own context window).
There is also compaction
(auto-summarizing older history, **one-way and not reversible**) · checkpoints / rewind ·
`/sessions` for session management. The CLI additionally has an experimental knowledge base (semantic retrieval).

**Concrete context-window numbers are not broken out in the official docs.**
(compaction and models pages checked.)
axes.permissions:
**Permissions are capability-based, not a two-state trust/untrust model.** Rules are written in YAML,
configured per capability with match / exclude, effect taking `deny` / `ask` / `allow`,
with precedence **deny > ask > allow**.

Capabilities listed officially:

- Files: `fs_read` / `fs_write`
- Execution: `shell` / `sandbox_network`
- Networking: `web_fetch` / `web_search`
- Extensions: `mcp` / `subagent` / `skill` / `power`
- Other: `context` / `diagnostics`

Six scopes in total: Kiro hardcoded, administration, user, workspace, agent, session.

The IDE additionally has Agent Autonomy with Autopilot / Supervised tiers.
**Workspaces are untrusted by default.** Before trust, repo-local agents, steering, MCP and Skills are not loaded.
**In headless mode, every `ask` is treated as `deny`.**

**Official permissions page wording**: capability-based, "replacing older binary trust models"
axes.fit:
Fits three kinds of people:

- Teams doing formal engineering delivery in the AWS ecosystem who want "spec first, implementation second"
- **People who need cloud sessions to keep running after shutdown** (Cloud sessions, up to 10 concurrent)
- Teams that want steering and permission rules **distributed with the repo** (`.kiro/` is committable, consistent across surfaces)

For a low-volume trial, the Free tier suffices: 50 credits per month, limited to open-weight models and Sonnet 4.5.

**Does not fit** two kinds of people. First, those wanting to plug in their own API keys or run local models — neither the official models nor pricing pages has any BYOK statement. Second, heavy users who need transparent quota accounting — credits are consumed at model multipliers, and no "fixed request count" conversion is given officially.

sections.四个 surface，一个 harness:
The official pages state the form clearly — "one agent, available everywhere you work":

| surface | official positioning |
|---|---|
| **IDE** | a standalone desktop IDE based on VS Code (built on a VS Code foundation) |
| **CLI** | a terminal TUI, plus headless mode for CI/CD |
| **Web** | a cloud agent in the browser, running in a hosted sandbox |
| **Mobile** | start and steer sessions from your phone |

**Key design: the IDE / CLI run the harness locally by default; Web / Mobile run in cloud sandboxes.**
But all four are front ends of the same harness, connected by the open protocol **ACP**.
Hence the official claim that JetBrains IDEs and Zed can also use Kiro as their agent.
sections.招牌：spec-driven development:
The official homepage wording: turn a prompt into "requirements, architectural designs, and sequenced tasks". Each spec lands as three files:

- `requirements.md` (or `bugfix.md`) — user stories and acceptance criteria
- `design.md` — technical architecture, sequence diagrams and implementation considerations
- `tasks.md` — discrete trackable tasks, supporting wave-parallel execution along the dependency graph

The supporting cast includes **steering files** (persistent project context in `.kiro/steering/`, four inclusion modes) and **agent hooks** (a dozen-plus trigger points, from File Save to Pre Task Execution).
